headline: First 300 tracks in — the run is deep in the rap/R&B album folders, and the data already shows it: vocal-forward, minor-key, trap-tempo. The electronic crates come later, and the picture will shift hard.
insights: 98% vocal across the first 300 tracks — exactly as expected. The run analyzes folders roughly alphabetically, so it's currently inside the rap/R&B albums (1017 Thug → Chilombo). Watch the vocal gauge fall off a cliff once it reaches the electronic Singles crate.

Tempo is already bimodal: a dense trap cluster at 130–152 BPM (the 136 and 144 spikes are textbook Atlanta half-time) plus a slower 96–118 R&B pocket. No house yet — that whole 122–128 spike arrives with the Singles.
Keys skew hard minor (12A, 7A, 5A on top) — the dark, moody harmonic fingerprint of trap and alt-R&B. Expect the major (B) Camelot codes to climb sharply once dance material enters the mix.

Mid energy (0.55) with low danceability (0.32) — this is melodic, atmospheric rap, not club fuel. It's the 'journey'-arc zone; the hype/Boiler-Room sets will crystallize later from the tech-house and baile crates.
The genre-anchored BPM correction is doing its job — trap tracks are landing in the 130–150 band instead of getting mis-detected at half-time (65–75).
roadblocks_note: Benign: librosa logs 'PySoundFile failed → trying audioread' for .m4a/.mp3 — that's the expected ffmpeg decode path, not an error. 0 failed decodes, 0 pull failures, device steady.
next: Next cycle should catch the transition out of the album block into Singles — the moment vocal% drops and house tempos appear.
